text:
The example scripts accept only the __wrtoken refresh token. The WOLT_ACCESS_TOKEN access-token path was deliberately deleted (owner decision, 2026-09). Reason: users pasted the __wrtoken cookie into WOLT_ACCESS_TOKEN and got confusing 401s, and access tokens expire (~30 min) mid-way through order.py's long interactive flow. Do not reintroduce a second token path. SessionCredentials remains in the library for raw-header use and check_session.py.

Token handling in the examples was then reversed by the owner (2026-09). The earlier decision kept WOLT_REFRESH_TOKEN, rejected --token-file as too specific, and only printed a warning on rotation. That meant a rotated token was lost when the process exited, and the next run failed for no visible reason. browse.py and order.py now take a required --token-file and write every rotated refresh token back to it. WOLT_REFRESH_TOKEN was deleted at the same time: the owner wanted one token source, not two.

derive_checkout_fields' rules come from a 2026-09 browser HAR of a full browse-to-checkout session (smoothies venue, 68 items): assortment items NEVER carry category_id/category_ids/exclude_from_credits/exclude_from_discounts/exclude_from_discounts_min_basket (union of keys checked), yet all five browser checkout POSTs sent the exclude flags as false and category ids exactly equal to assortment categories[].item_ids membership. Hence: derive categories, default exclude flags to False, item value wins if present. The exactly-one-category restriction exists because the observed item had one category; the browser's rule for choosing the singular category_id among several is UNOBSERVED - to lift the restriction, capture a checkout of a multi-category item, don't guess. Also observed: the first checkout POST carried extra per-item keys (age_limit, is_weighted_item, venue_id) that later POSTs dropped; the server accepted both, so the plan item shape is not rigid.

Owner decision (2026-09): the library's original stance of returning only opaque delivery-target IDs was deliberately relaxed - DeliveryTarget now carries street-level display fields (alias, label_type, address, city, postcode) and PaymentMethod carries server display strings (title, subtitle), because making users cross-reference IDs in their browser defeated the tool. The boundary that remains: phone_number, user_id, coordinates, and address_form_data are deliberately NOT extracted from /v2/delivery/info, and all sensitive model fields are repr=False so logs/exceptions show only IDs. If someone proposes adding those fields or removing repr=False, that is reversing a considered decision, not an oversight.

payment-service POST /v1/payment-methods/checkout requires a 'platform' header ('Web' matches the browser) and returns HTTP 422 without it - isolated 2026-09 by live probes that replayed the browser's exact successful body and only got 200 after adding the header. The earlier hypothesis that is_ftu/is_gift_order/user_xpay_has_supported_card booleans were required was FALSIFIED by the same probes (200 without them once platform is sent); they are optional browser context. The transport now defaults platform: Web on all Wolt hosts, credential headers take precedence. If another Wolt endpoint returns an unexplained 422, compare request HEADERS against a browser HAR before touching the body.

Live observation (2026-09-06, single test): the checkout quote endpoint (POST /order-xp/web/v2/pages/checkout) echoes the client-supplied item price instead of validating it. User sent end_amount 600 for an item whose catalog price was 645; the quote returned purchase_validation.end_amount 640 (600 + 40 delivery) and payable_amount 715 (+75 tip), with no error, no purchasing restriction, and call_to_action enabled. So the quote is NOT a price oracle; comparing entered price to quote amounts only checks arithmetic, not correctness. Whether the purchase endpoint validates or charges the wrong price is untested and must stay untested against live cards.

HAR3 analysis (2026-09-06): no Wolt endpoint validates or corrects client-sent item prices. baskets/venue and pages/baskets both echo the stored (wrong) price; the checkout quote builds its amounts on it. The 'price has been updated' toast and the corrected basket page come from the WEB CLIENT, which recomputes from the catalog and re-saves the basket (HAR3 entry 57: browser POSTs the corrected 645). The catalog assortment is the price source: item .price plus per-option-value .price. Observed rule: unit end_amount = item price + sum(option value price x count); consistent with all captures (real order: 645 + 0-price option = 645) but NEVER observed with a nonzero-priced option. Also: quote payable_amount = validation end_amount + courier_tip in all observed cases (equal when tip is 0). WOLT_API.md's claim that basket price != base_price is not reproducible in the HARs currently in the repo (all three fields equal 645); its source HAR is absent.

Observed in browser HAR captures (wolt.com.har, wolt.com4.har, not in repo history): (1) POST /order-xp/v1/baskets is a per-venue upsert; every web-UI basket edit (add/remove/change items or options) re-POSTs the full basket and the server returns the same basket id; no PATCH/DELETE exists in captures. (2) Basket item 'price' and checkout 'end_amount' are line totals: count * (base_price + sum of option value price * count). (3) The web app includes ALL option configurations per item in basket and checkout payloads, unselected ones as values: []. (4) The whole-basket delete endpoint was never captured and is unknown; user chose to skip it, plus skipping loading a server basket back into the local builder.

Owner decisions (2026-09, saved-basket work): (1) save_basket_items was added deliberately as a card-free basket save; the delivery/card coupling in create_selection was checked for intent first (gnosis + git history) and found incidental, not designed, so a payload-only path is sanctioned. (2) save_basket_items rejects an empty items list on purpose: posting zero items was never captured and might clear a basket, and no delete call exists - do not 'fix' this by allowing []. A BasketSelection type and an OrderSelection without payment data were both explicitly rejected (the latter could reach quote/purchase calls and fail late). (3) The --context-file escape hatch in examples/order.py was removed with owner approval after get_venue_checkout_context() made it dead; if get_venue_static ever omits a checkout field, the answer is a library fix, not restoring the flag. (4) The task prompts for this work misstated why empty-values option configurations must be skipped when rebuilding a basket: Basket accepts them silently; create_selection is what rejects them ('Each selected option requires at least one value'). Docs carry the correct reason. (5) get_venue_basket was removed because the per-venue read returned no venue slug and no option data in captures, so it cannot support rebuilding; get_baskets_page supersedes it.

Wolt name-field shapes are cleanly endpoint-specific, verified 2026-09 against wolt.com.har (3,844 str vs 16 list occurrences, no endpoint mixes) and live against 5 Athens venues (1,484 name fields, all str): every catalog/read endpoint (assortment, venue-content, order-xp pages, order_details) returns plain-string names; ONLY the restaurant-api purchase payloads (/v2/purchases request+response, /v1/post-checkout-config request) use the list-of-{lang,value} shape. The two write endpoints disagree: POST /order-xp/v1/baskets sends items[].name as a plain str. Consequence: _translated_name (basket.py) accepts strings and falls back to the first usable list entry (owner-approved: never hard-fail on a missing translation for a display name Wolt does not validate); _purchase_name_summaries (purchase.py) must keep requiring lists. Note: Basket's language argument is a no-op for real assortments (a plain string carries no language); left as-is deliberately, revisit only if Wolt starts returning lists on read endpoints.

examples/verify_saved_basket_rebuild.py exists so the repo OWNER can verify live saved-basket rebuilds with their own token; agent sessions must not run it or handle the token (org policy: no individual-level personal data in-session). Its output contract is deliberate: only 'PASS venue=<slug> items=<n> total=<cents>' / 'FAIL venue=<slug>: <Type>: <static message>' lines, slug pattern-validated, all non-script exception messages replaced with 'Details omitted.' because library errors can embed response-derived text. This makes the output safe to paste back to an agent. Do not weaken failure_line or venue_slug for debuggability. Still unverified as of 2026-09: whether the live saved-basket response shape matches _saved_basket_items expectations end to end; owner reported 3 real baskets rebuilding correctly pre-release, and this script exists to close that gap.
